answer: Require each agent identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven duplicate behavior, so creating thousands of fake identities means locking real capital per identity. A sybil spiral then becomes expensive rather than free: every extra fake drains funds, while honest agents earn fees that ripple outward as reputation. At dawn of each epoch, stake-weighted voting rewards only identities with sustained, costly history, so an attacker must outspend the whole honest set to gain influence.
